newsitem.title: INDIA: India business wants liberalised insurance sector.
newsitem.headline: India business wants liberalised insurance sector.

text.p: Indian businessmen on Thursday urged that the nation's insurance industry be opened to private enterprise in order to provide the huge funds required to shore up the crumbling infrastructure sector.

The Bombay Chamber of Commerce and Industry (BCCI) said in a white paper on infrastructure development that India should follow global practice and tap long term contractual savings like insurance and provident funds to provide money to the infrastructure sector.
"The Indian insurance sector should be opened up in line with the Malhotra Committee recommendations," the paper, made available to Reuters, said.
"This will help the development of a long-term debt market which is a prerequisite for the successful implementation of long-term funding."

The BCCI estimated that India would have to invest over $100 billion by the turn of the century to meet its needs in just the power and telecommunications sectors alone. Upgrading roads and ports would require hundreds of millions of dollars more.
The Malhotra report is a blueprint for the opening-up of India's state-controlled insurance sector, dominated since 1956 by the Life Insurance Corp (LIC) and the General Insurance Corp (GIC).
The BCCI white paper advised the government to enact legislation to permit the LIC to invest its holdings in infrastructure.

"LIC, for instance, has investible funds of $18.57 billion, most of which is directed into government/quasigovernment debt," the study said. "A small legislative change that frees the funds from directed government lending would open up enormous funds for infrastructure."
Insurance firms will also be able to provide counter-guarantees for infrastructure projects, the study said.
